summary: The two top-performing clips (354K and 255K views) both use a single relatable 'you/us' meme sentence that stays on screen for the entire clip — the text IS the joke, the footage is just atmosphere. The hook names a specific date (November 19th) or a universally shared gamer tension, which triggers immediate self-identification. Sentence-case white text, centered, no subtitles, no voiceover, just 3 slowly-cutting Vice City/GTA 6 trailer shots behind one static punchline. Rank 3 (15K) used the same formula but picked a narrower scenario (sneaking from girlfriend) that alienated non-gamers and shot in a dark, low-contrast scene — proving visual readability and broad relatability are what separate top from mid.
moments_to_pick: Broad 'us gamers' meme tied to the November 19th launch date — the more people who can see themselves in it, the better
PC vs console tension moments (e.g., PC players locked out, 30fps jokes) — highest relatability in ranks 1 & 2
Jason & Lucia couple dynamic used as a stand-in for a real-life relationship meme (e.g., choosing GTA 6 over a partner)
Vice City neon/nightlife b-roll shots for visual atmosphere behind a static joke — colorful, high-contrast frames only
Hype countdown moments: anything framing the 19th as an event bigger than a holiday or life milestone
Platform/regional divide memes (console vs PC, country pricing, New Zealand trick) — trending hard per YouTube data
hook_examples: Us on November 19th calling in sick with 'food poisoning': 🤒
POV: GTA 6 just dropped and you're still at work pretending to care:
Jason and Lucia watching PC players wait 2 more years: 💀
Every gamer on the planet November 19th at 12:01 AM:
The way GTA 6 is about to make therapy appointments go up 📈
Bro said he doesn't care about GTA 6. Bro has not seen the graphics 😭
title_formula: [Relatable gamer scenario] + specific detail that stings (platform, date, fps number) + 1-2 emojis. Keep under 60 chars. E.g.: 'PC Players On November 19th 😭🖥️' or 'GTA 6 Has Us Calling In Sick 💀'
caption_formula: 1 short punchy sentence mirroring the on-screen joke (do NOT repeat it word for word — rephrase or add context) + line break + '🎵 Tokyo Girl — Miri Ben-Ari' (song credit required by campaign rules) + line break + hashtag block. Keep the whole caption under 150 chars excluding hashtags.
avoid: Dark, low-contrast shots where text becomes hard to read — rank 3's bedroom scene hurt readability badly
Scenarios too niche to relate to (sneaking from a specific partner type, regional jokes only 1 country gets)
Splitting the joke across 3 separate text beats — top clips hold ONE sentence the whole 12s; punching it up per beat loses the punchline
Putting the song title or credit inside the on-screen text overlay — keep credit in caption only per campaign rules
Voiceover, dialogue audio, or any sound other than Tokyo Girl added in TikTok/IG
Using footage from other creators' edits — only original GTA 6 trailer/gameplay sourced clips
experiment: Try a 3-beat escalating text structure on ONE clip this cycle: Beat 1 sets the relatable setup (e.g., 'You on November 19th:'), Beat 2 adds the twist ('Your boss:'), Beat 3 lands the punchline ('The hospital bill:') — each beat synced to a new shot cut.
